summary: Describes a high-level meeting location policy for the IETF and the stakeholders needed to carry it out.

plainLanguage.summary: This is a short guide on where and how the IETF decides to hold its in-person gatherings.

questions: what is an ietf exploratory meeting
subtitle: The 1-1-1-* policy for rotating IETF meetings between North America, Europe and Asia.

tldr.problem: The IETF aimed to spread meetings equally across regions, but the policy had never been defined precisely or documented in a consensus document.
tldr.mechanism: Meetings should rotate between North America, Europe and Asia over the long term, with an extra exploratory meeting (the asterisk) allowed for experiments such as other regions or virtual meetings.
tldr.outcome: The IASA treats the policy as an aspiration of the community when it selects venues using the process in RFC 8718.

today: RFC 8719 is a Best Current Practice (BCP 226) and is updated by RFC 9712.

sections.title: Why a Meeting Policy
sections.content:
IETF work happens mainly on working group mailing lists. Face-to-face meetings are mostly a high-bandwidth way to work out unresolved issues. The IETF strives for a 1-1-1 policy: distribute meetings equally between North America, Europe and Asia, where most participants have come from recently.

The rotation spreads travel effort for people who attend in person and timezone difficulty for remote participants. The policy had not been precisely defined or documented in a consensus document until this BCP.
sections.plainLanguage: Most of the work happens by email. Meetings help with the hard bits, and moving them around shares the long trips fairly.

sections.title: The 1-1-1-* Policy
sections.content:
Meetings should rotate between North America, Europe and Asia. The boundaries between those regions are deliberately left undefined. Balance is judged over several years, not each year, so a given year need not follow a fixed cycle, and later years should seek to rebalance.

The asterisk adds an exploratory meeting: a flexible slot for experiments such as meetings in other regions, virtual meetings, or extra meetings beyond the three regular ones in a calendar year. Their timing and frequency depend on IETF consensus as determined by the IETF chair. IETF 95 in Buenos Aires and IETF 47 in Adelaide are named as exceptional instances.
sections.plainLanguage: Take turns between three regions, and once in a while try something different, like a far-off place or an online meeting.

sections.title: How the Policy Is Carried Out
sections.content:
The IETF Administrative Support Activity (IASA) is to treat the policy as the aspiration of the community. It selects the venue using the process in RFC 8718 and helps develop detailed meeting criteria and keeps the community informed so feedback can be acted upon.

Because geography strongly influences venue choice, it is to be considered at the same level as the other Important Criteria in RFC 8718. This can include trading off the region against other criteria, and telling the community if the region requirement cannot be met.
sections.plainLanguage: The people who book the venue treat the turn-taking rule as a goal, and tell everyone if they cannot meet it.

sections.title: Proposing Exploratory Meetings and Revising the Policy
sections.content:
Anyone interested in an exploratory venue proposes it on the IETF discussion list or a list set up for the purpose. If the IETF chair finds community consensus to pursue it, the venue goes to the venue-selection mailing list for refinement. The IESG decides in consultation with the IASA, and the final decision is communicated back for comment.

Participant distribution changes over time, so the policy is expected to be re-evaluated periodically. The community should agree the criteria first, for example mirroring draft author distribution over the preceding five years.
sections.plainLanguage: If someone wants a special trip, they suggest it, everyone comments, and the leaders decide and explain why.

references.text: Haberman, B., Hall, J., and J. Livingood, "Structure of the IETF Administrative Support Activity, Version 2.0", BCP 101, RFC 8711, February 2020.
Lear, E., Ed., "IETF Plenary Meeting Venue Selection Process", BCP 226, RFC 8718, February 2020.
